deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is folio 34 of Gauss's running correspondence and postage ledger for the second half of 1815, continuing the January–June 1815 page before it (headed 'Von … An … Cassen').

Layout:
- Column 1: date and correspondent of letters received ('Von').
- Column 2: correspondents of letters sent ('An').
- Two money columns, each in Groschen and Pfennig, 12 Pf = 1 Gr. These appear to be postage, perhaps one column paid out of pocket and one charged to the university/observatory account ('Cassen'); this reading is uncertain.

Correspondents named include Wynecken, Nicolai, v. Lindenau, Sander, Bessel, Olbers, Jacobi, Gerling, Fraunhofer, Bode, Meineke, Waldeck, Pfaff, Struve, Encke, v. Utzschneider, the Curator, Pasquich, Kuntze, Ahrenschildt, Möbius, Buquoy, Laplace, Harding, Wehrs and Münster.

The only 'computations' are period subtotals.

July: 14 received, 7 sent, right money column 16 Gr 0 Pf.

August: 16 received, 9 sent.
- Middle column 3 Gr 10 Pf (one entry, Waldeck/Pfaff).
- Right column 7 Gr 7 Pf. This checks: 0;2 + 1;6 + 0;2 + 0;6 + 4;9 + 0;2 + 0;2 + 0;2 = 5 Gr 31 Pf = 7 Gr 7 Pf.

September to 14 October: 14 received, 10 sent.
- Middle column 4 Gr 0 Pf = 3;10 + 0;2.
- Right column 9 Gr 8 Pf = 3;2 + 3;2 + 0;2 + 3;2.

Running totals entered under that block: 123 letters received, 7 Gr 10 Pf, and 33 Gr 3 Pf.
- 123 = 79 (Jan–Jun total from the previous page) + 14 + 16 + 14.
- 7;10 = 3;10 + 4;0.
- 33;3 = 16;0 + 7;7 + 9;8.

Mid-October to mid-December: the right column (entries 0;2, 0;2, 3;0, 0;2, 0;2, 6;4, 0;2, 2;10, 0;2, 1;6, 0;2, 0;6, 3;2, 2;10, 0;4, 0;2, 0;4, 0;2) sums to 17 Gr 64 Pf = 22 Gr 4 Pf. This matches the written subtotal '22 4'.

Late-December entries (9 10, 1 6) follow below the rule as a new running block.
errors: July: the right-column entries I can read (4;8, 0;2, 3;2, 0;2, 0;2, 0;2, 1;6) sum to only 10 Gr 0 Pf, but the subtotal reads 16 Gr. The running total 33;3 is consistent with 16;0, so Gauss used 16. Either an entry is misread or illegible on my side, or Gauss slipped and carried the slip forward. This cannot be resolved from the image.
No other arithmetic errors: the August, September/October, cumulative and Oct–Dec totals all check.

results.what: Bookkeeping of correspondence and postage (letters received/sent with fees in Groschen/Pfennig, subtotals per period)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely administrative: a postage and correspondence ledger. It has documentary value for Gauss's 1815 correspondence network but no mathematical content.

checkable.asserts: August right-column entries sum to 7 Gr 7 Pf (12 Pf = 1 Gr)
September/early October right column sums to 9 Gr 8 Pf
September middle column sums to 4 Gr 0 Pf
Cumulative count of received letters through mid-October
Cumulative right-column total 33 Gr 3 Pf using July = 16 Gr
Visible July entries sum to only 10 Gr 0 Pf, not the written 16 Gr
Oct–Dec right-column entries sum to 22 Gr 4 Pf

transcription_corrections: 'Enouy' in the image is Encke (the transcription's 'Encke' is correct).
The October 19 entry 'aus Greifsw.' has money entry 3 Gr in the right column (with dashes in the middle columns), not '— 3 —' as one amount.
The July Wynecken entries are dated 12, 16, 17 (three received letters), which explains the count of 14 for July.
Sept 17 'An' entry reads 'Weingarten(?) Sander' as two names; 'Weingarten' is uncertain.
Dec 15 struck-through name, transcribed '[-Pfaff[?]-]', is illegible on my reading.
'Wynecken' July 24/27 entries are faint; the second faint entry (25) is Gerling, consistent with the transcription.
